clue.text: Labours to replenish the dairy farmer's stock

definitions.meaning: a cow that labours gives birth, which the farming verb for a cow delivering young names

definitions.text: to replenish the dairy farmer's stock
definitions.meaning: young cattle born on the farm restock a dairy herd

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means a cow giving birth; as a plural noun it is the young cattle that refill a dairy herd.

clue.text: Threw the club, the case being unbreakable

parts.note: to cast is to throw
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Someone hurls a golf club in a fit of temper, but the club's head is too tough to break.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as made of this metal, figuratively, is rigid and impossible to shatter or overturn, as in a firm alibi.

clue.text: Show this for giving together

parts.note: read 'for giving' as one word, forgiving: the quality you show when you forgive someone

explanation.walkthrough: Close the gap in 'for giving' (the 'together' tells you to) and the clue asks what quality you show in forgiving: mercy or mildness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildness and mercy shown to a wrongdoer is what forgiving someone involves.

clue.text: A novel governess…

parts.note: the title heroine of Charlotte Bronte's 1847 novel works as governess at Thornfield Hall

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 5-down: Charlotte Bronte wrote the novel, and her sister Anne used the pen name Acton Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane, the title character of Charlotte Bronte's novel, is employed as a governess to Rochester's ward.

clue.text: Simple social worker immersed in growth of bird seed

indicators.note: the insect is sunk inside the word for simple

parts.note: plain means simple
an ant is a worker in a social insect colony

explanation.surface: A humble social worker is buried in a patch of birdseed.
explanation.definitionFit: This weed is grown for its seed spikes, which are fed to cage birds.

clue.text: … And acton Bell's relationship to her producer

definitions.text: And acton Bell's relationship to her producer

parts.words: And acton Bell's relationship to her producer
parts.note: Acton Bell was the pen name of Anne Bronte, the youngest sibling of Charlotte, who produced the governess novel of 3-down

explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' refers back to the governess of 3-down, so her producer is her author, Charlotte Bronte; Anne (Acton Bell) was Charlotte's younger sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Bronte was younger than Charlotte, so she was the younger female sibling of the novelist.

clue.text: Article has nothing about point of fixture

indicators.note: nothing is placed round the article, so the word for zero wraps the letter

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A reporter's piece contains no comment on a key moment of a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal spike hammered in is the thing that holds a fixing in place, a fastening at a single point.

clue.text: Seem a very quiet listener

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone appears to be a calm, attentive audience for a friend's troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem a certain way is to look or come across that way to an observer.

clue.text: Would this type of canal boat measure up to the Broads?

definitions.text: Would this type of canal boat measure up to the Broads?

parts.words: Would this type of canal boat measure up to the Broads?
parts.note: a slim canal boat is set against the Norfolk Broads, whose name suggests width, so the boat type is the opposite of broad

explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are English lakes and waterways popular for boating; 'Broads' also says wide, and the canal boat is named for being slim.
explanation.definitionFit: The long thin boats built for English canals are named for being slim, the opposite of broad.

clue.text: Half of us on door watch

indicators.note: one of the two letters of the short word is taken, its first

parts.note: a door is an entry into a building

explanation.surface: Half of a household stands guard at the front door.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard posted to keep watch is a sentinel on duty.

clue.text: Sunny start and excursionist readily peels off

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word Sunny is taken

parts.note: a tripper is someone on a day excursion

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker on a sunny day strips off clothes the moment the sun comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: one who peels off clothes readily, as in a striptease act.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertainer whose act is removing clothes is someone who takes them off without hesitation.

clue.text: One can find something left to be salvaged

definitions.text: One can find something left to be salvaged

parts.words: One can find something left to be salvaged
parts.note: a consoling phrase said when, despite a setback, there is still something to save

explanation.definitionFit: The saying offers hope that a situation is still recoverable because some remnant survives.

clue.text: Evergreen as one Roman law

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
lex is the Latin word for law

explanation.surface: A tree that stays green is likened to the constant law of ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The holm oak and holly genus are shrubs and trees that keep their leaves all year.

clue.text: How surreptitiously Christopher watched a shrewish performance?

definitions.text: How surreptitiously Christopher watched a shrewish performance?

parts.words: How surreptitiously Christopher watched a shrewish performance?
parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker for whom the play of The Taming of the Shrew is staged, so his surname turned adverb describes how he watched

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew a drunk named Christopher Sly is tricked into watching the play; add -LY to his surname for an adverb meaning surreptitiously.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a cunning, secretive way is the adverb for acting stealthily.

clue.text: Castlebar's county mayor cut off

indicators.note: the civic leader's title loses its final letter, chopped away at the tail

explanation.surface: In an Irish town, the civic leader is cut off by his own county.
explanation.walkthrough: Castlebar is the county town of an Irish county in the west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Castlebar is the administrative seat of this western Irish county.

clue.text: The fishing vessel to strike?

definitions.meaning: a single-masted sailing boat used for fishing

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a traditional sailing boat used for fishing and a verb for hitting with an open hand.

clue.text: Nine daredevil performers ?

definitions.meaning: a group of nine musicians or a piece for nine players
trapeze artists who work without a safety mesh beneath them

explanation.walkthrough: Split the letters as two words, NO NET: the condition of high-wire acts who perform without a safety net.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nine performers is a musical ensemble term; read as two words it describes acrobats working without a safety net.

clue.text: Serving with an appointed body for a percentage (2, 10) 201 drop out as actress Eileen becomes an up stager

definitions.meaning: sitting as a member of a commission, a body set up for a task
paid a percentage of each sale rather than a salary

explanation.definitionFit: A salesman paid this way earns a share of each deal; a member of an official board is working on that panel.

clue.text: A red flier possibly blazing away at nothing

parts.note: flaming means burning, blazing away
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A gunner fires away at nothing in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blazing away' suggests shooting, but it means burning; 'possibly' marks the definition as an example, a pink wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This pink-red wading bird is one example of a coloured bird in flight.

clue.text: Boastful brat holding up horseplay with gravity

indicators.note: the naughty child's letters contain the reversed piece
in a down clue the letters for horseplay and gravity are read upward, backwards

parts.note: a rag is a boisterous prank, horseplay
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A bratty child disrupts serious play with rough horseplay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' in a down clue turns the horseplay-and-gravity pair to read upward; 'holding' puts that turned pair inside the naughty child, after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart is a boaster; used attributively the word describes boasting behaviour.

clue.text: I drop out as actress Eileen becomes an upstager

indicators.note: the letter is removed from the pool as the rest is reworked; 'becomes' links the fodder to the result

parts.note: taken as written for the letter pool
the personal pronoun, removed from the pool

explanation.surface: An actress named Eileen quits a production and turns into a performer who steals the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: The I was printed at the end of 17-across's run-on text ('201' = '20 I'). Remove I from ACTRESS EILEEN and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who draws attention away from fellow performers is said to upstage them.

clue.text: Had a suitable try-on?

parts.note: a try-on at a tailor's is a fitting, so having one suitably is being measured for clothes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Try-on' in slang is an attempted trick, but here it is a session trying clothes at a tailor's.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor's trying of a garment is a session that makes it match the body.

clue.text: A capital place to talk turkey?

definitions.text: A capital place to talk turkey?

parts.words: A capital place to talk turkey?
parts.note: the seat of government of the country Turkey, where national business is discussed; 'talk turkey' means speak frankly

explanation.definitionFit: This city is the seat of government of the Turkish republic.

clue.text: Where barristers get their refreshers?

parts.note: refreshers are extra fees paid to barristers and also drinks

explanation.walkthrough: A refresher is a further fee paid to a British barrister in a long case; the four Inns of Court are the barristers' professional societies, and an inn is also a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs serve refreshments, and the barristers' professional bodies are called Inns of Court.

clue.text: Head stableboy drove off with a spirited horse

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word stableboy is used

parts.note: in golf, to drive off is to tee off, so teed means drove off

explanation.surface: The head stable lad rode away on a lively mount.
explanation.definitionFit: A mount, especially a lively one, is a literary word for a horse.

clue.text: One might feel choked by such a dirty blanket

definitions.text: One might feel choked by such a dirty blanket

parts.words: One might feel choked by such a dirty blanket
parts.note: a pall of polluted fog covering a city, choking those beneath it

explanation.definitionFit: Polluted fog lies over a city like a grimy covering and makes breathing hard.

clue.text: False god often screened

definitions.meaning: an image worshipped as a deity
a film star seen on screen often, a screen favourite

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a worshipped image and a celebrated film star.

clue.text: Plug for street operation

explanation.surface: A road repair calls for a bung to block a burst pipe in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To plug a hole is to block it up.

clue.text: Could it be a dramatic let-down for a 20?

definitions.text: Could it be a dramatic let-down for a 20?

parts.words: Could it be a dramatic let-down for a 20?
parts.note: a hinged opening in a stage floor could drop the upstaging performer of 20-across out of sight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Let-down' suggests disappointment, but a stage opening literally lets an actor down below.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged panel in a stage floor lowers actors out of view.

clue.text: Held by the first Anzac lines

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something is held by the first Australian and New Zealand troops in the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A verse of a poem is a group of lines.

clue.text: Make many sketches and pull out the winner by chance

definitions.meaning: produce a large number of drawings

definitions.text: pull out the winner by chance
definitions.meaning: decide by picking tickets or straws at random

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it is to sketch a great deal; as an idiom it is to choose by random selection.

clue.text: Shoot that could make upper-class sport

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged to make something new

parts.note: U denotes upper-class

explanation.surface: Grouse shooting could be seen as the upper-class sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A new growth from a plant is a young stem.
